chunks: And it is narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who made an advance payment for something in which people make advance payments, from fruits, but its fruits were lost, and he did not fully receive his advance.
He عليه السلام said: “Then let him take his principal capital, or let him grant him respite.”

key_terms.أَسْلَفَ: he made an advance payment in a salam-type transaction
key_terms.الثِّمَارِ: fruits used here as the example commodity
key_terms.سَلَفَهُ: his advance payment or prepaid entitlement
key_terms.لِيُنْظِرْهُ: to give him more time or respite

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if goods bought through advance payment are destroyed before delivery?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on an advance-payment sale when the contracted fruits are destroyed before delivery. The buyer is entitled to recover his original capital, or he may choose to grant the seller additional time.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3938 - It is narrated from Abdullah bin Bukayr, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (as) about a man who made an advance payment (salam) for something that people typically make advance payments for, such as fruits, but the fruits were destroyed, and he did not receive what was due.
Imam (as) said: "Let him take back his principal amount, or he may grant the debtor more time."
